title: Keep a --render failure inside one JSON envelope
lead:
A mutating handler emits its success JSON, then `_mutating` runs `render.write`.
If rendering raises (e.g. a template referencing an unknown placeholder), the
exception propagates to `main`, which prints a *second* JSON error envelope and
exits 2 — after the mutation is already committed. Agents parsing stdout as one
JSON document mis-handle it, and the non-zero exit misrepresents a mutation that
actually succeeded.
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** changing what `render` itself writes, or its standalone
command behavior.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The agent contract (docs/agents.md) promises a single JSON document to stdout
and an exit code that reflects the outcome. Two documents plus a misleading exit
code on the common "broken template" case breaks that contract.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — `_mutating` (~lines 47-67) and the handlers' `_emit`
- `src/slicer/render.py` — `RenderError` is the failure raised
- `tests/test_render.py` or `tests/test_cli.py`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A mutating command with `--render` and a deliberately broken template writes
   the mutation, then emits exactly one JSON document describing the render
   failure, with a defined exit code.
2. The happy path still emits one success envelope and renders.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Restructure `_mutating` so rendering happens before the success payload is
emitted, or so a render failure is folded into the single envelope (mutation
succeeded, render failed, as a warning field), never a second document. Decide
and document the exit code for "mutation ok, render failed". Keep the plain
(non-`--json`) output equally coherent.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`--json` mutations with `--render` always produce one parseable document; the
exit code matches the documented meaning whether render succeeds or fails.
